description: Every configuration key the mailbox reads, with its starting value. Each key names its one reader: `core` (fgos-mailbox-core, `Limits`) or `hook` (fgos-mailbox, `HookLimits`). This file is the only place these values live: neither crate has a numeric constant or a default, so a missing key is a load error. Values are the starting values of docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md section 12, unmeasured on fgOS. Status keys are added by the rung that reads them.

keys.meaning: size cap of a message body; a larger body is refused and the sender is told to send a path or link
chain depth cap, counted on the derived reply chain only
agent-origin send attempts by one sender inside the rolling window; refused attempts count too
send attempts by one sender generation over its whole life, never reset
the rolling window of the session budget, used on every CLI instead of a human-input signal
messages between one ordered pair inside the loop window before the loop guard refuses
length of the loop guard window
pending messages per recipient; the newest is refused when full
pending messages one sender may hold in one recipient's queue
size bound of the per-party refusal and notice counters in a snapshot; the least recently bumped entry is evicted
a message still recorded after this age is refused with a notice
the body of an offered or refused message is dropped this long after its last state change
time an unfinished claim hides a message; must exceed the adapters' measured latency
offers per message before it is refused with a notice
a silence of at least this long between two heads starts a new exchange
wake sends that take effect within one exchange, both directions together
wake sends that took effect by one sender generation to one recipient, never reset
notices held per address; the oldest is dropped on overflow
at most one notice per (sender, reason) inside this window
length bound of a frame header value, and so of a short name and of a writer key the core accepts
keys.status: placeholder borrowed from session identity's MAX_ID_LENGTH, unmeasured

keys.meaning: consecutive Stop blocks that were written and finished for one head generation; the count returns to zero when a Stop passes without blocking or a new turn starts
longest wait for the mailbox lock before a hook skips its drain
